title: Machine learning detects volcanic fingerprints and suggests a northern extratropical signal for the unidentified 1809 eruption
summary: A convolutional neural network trained on idealized Earth-system-model simulations classified eruption occurrence and broad latitude band from global surface-temperature anomalies in the first post-eruption summer. Applied to reanalysis and observational climate records, the method identified major historic events and assigned a northern-extratropical footprint to the unidentified 1809 eruption. The same analysis found that some smaller events leave weaker, less distinguishable temperature signals.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network with explainable-AI relevance mapping
organization: German Climate Computing Center (DKRZ); Max Planck Institute for Meteorology; Center for Climate Physics, Institute for Basic Science; Pusan National University

evidence.tested: A convolutional neural network trained on idealized Earth-system-model simulations classified eruption occurrence and broad latitude band from global surface-temperature anomalies in the first post-eruption summer.
evidence.unknown: The model is trained on idealized simulations with only three broad eruption latitude classes and four sulfur-injection strengths. The 1809 geographic inference is an AI classification of a climate fingerprint, not direct observation of the eruption source; predictions show sensitivity to normalization and differing observational datasets. It should be interpreted as a clue, not a definitive eruption-location determination.
evidence.ai_role: The CNN classified volcanic presence/location using post-eruption temperature patterns; explainability analysis localized climate regions driving those classifications and helped infer the 1809 event’s northern-extratropical footprint from observational/reanalysis data.
